guarantees.claim: key_o is continuously assigned the value of signal regular.
out_req_o is assigned SP2V_HIGH when the bitwise AND reduction of sub_word_out_req is true (all bits 1), otherwise SP2V_LOW.

assumptions.claim: The reduction AND of sub_word_out_req accurately signals that all sub-word operations have completed their output request.
assumptions.cond: always, while key expansion is active
assumptions.risk: If any bit of sub_word_out_req is stuck at 0 or deasserted incorrectly, out_req_o will remain SP2V_LOW, causing a permanent stall of the key expansion output handshake.

assumptions.claim: SP2V_HIGH and SP2V_LOW are correctly defined sparse-encoding constants representing logical true and false respectively, matching the consumer's decoding.
assumptions.risk: If the constants are swapped or incorrect, the downstream logic may misinterpret an active request as inactive, leading to data loss or deadlock.

uncertain_points.claim: The definitions of SP2V_HIGH and SP2V_LOW are not visible in this chunk; the consumer's sparse decoding must be verified to match these constants.
uncertain_points.risk: If encoding mismatches, out_req_o may be permanently misinterpreted, breaking the handshake.

uncertain_points.claim: sub_word_out_req is a multi-bit vector; if any of its bits are combinational or subject to glitches, the reduction AND could produce transient false values on out_req_o, violating handshake stability.
uncertain_points.cond: when sub_word_out_req bits are not registered or synchronized
uncertain_points.risk: A glitch on out_req_o might cause a downstream consumer to sample an incorrect sparse value, potentially triggering a false handshake or protocol violation.
